chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaqan, who said:

I saw Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third [Imam] prostrating the prostration of gratitude, and he spread out his arms and pressed his chest and belly to the ground. So I asked him about that, and he said: 'Such is how we love to do it.'

key_terms.افْتَرَشَ: Spread out (referring to the posture of prostration)
key_terms.جُؤْجُؤُهُ: His chest (specifically the upper chest/breastbone area)

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam perform the prostration of gratitude according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Hassan al-Askari (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual significance of Sajdat al-Shukr, emphasizing total physical submission by pressing the chest and belly to the ground as an expression of profound gratitude. In Shia scholarly tradition, this act is viewed not merely as a ritual but as a manifestation of humility and recognition of divine favors, reinforcing the connection between physical posture and spiritual state.
